messages:
Meg (Platform): Heads-up: we need a decision on how hosted/dedicated/private runtimes obtain short-lived credentials and do cache eviction. Two patterns on the table: (A) control-plane mints scoped short-lived tokens and forwards to runtimes; (B) a tiny local sidecar that holds keys/KMS and exposes a minimal auth/evict API. I want to pick a default strategy and a fallback for tomorrow's rollout.

Sanjay: Strong preference for sidecar in Private due to HSM/KMS constraints. Control-plane should not see raw keys for regulated customers. Sidecar can sign ephemeral leases locally.

Tess: Sidecar + ops surface is a concern. For Hosted we won't run sidecars in the same way. We need a unified runtime acceptance policy so runtimes accept either token provenance uniformly.

Leo: Keep the sidecar API intentionally tiny. Proposed endpoints:
GET /auth?scope=<scope> => {token, expires_at}
POST /cache/invalidate => 204
GET /health => 200
That keeps semantics clear and language-agnostic.

Meg (Platform): Agreed. Runtime will accept either a token issued by sidecar or a control-plane-signed token. We must standardize claim keys: e.g., "capabilities" and "max_seq_len". Also add an HTTP header to indicate origin: X-Auth-Origin: sidecar|controlplane.

Sanjay: Important: sidecar must not attempt to perform batching/cache decisions. Runtime remains the authority for batching and KV cache lifecycle. Sidecar only provides token issuance and eviction commands.

Tess: Air-gapped Private clusters: bootstrap story? Options: manual CSR for sidecar certs or an offline signed token rotation process. For the first rollout, let's do manual CSR to keep it simple.

Leo: Manual CSR for initial rollout is fine. I'll draft a tiny protobuf for the auth lease so it's easy to implement across languages: message AuthLease { string token = 1; int64 expires_at = 2; repeated string capabilities = 3; } Keep it minimal.

Meg (Platform): Observability requirement: sidecar must emit token_issue_count and cache_invalidate_count. Control-plane mint path must map to the same metric names so billing joins don't diverge. Also include origin header on metrics.

Sanjay: Also surface a compatibility header so runtime can log which path was used and trigger fallback rules if necessary.

Tess: Proposal: run a short experiment — deploy a sidecar stub in one Dedicated cluster and use control-plane minting in Hosted for two weeks. Measure latency, ops overhead, and incident counts. If sidecar wins for Dedicated and Private, we extend it.

Meg (Platform): Action items:
- Tess: implement sidecar stub in dedicated env (ticket INF-2340)
- Leo: author protobuf + endpoint spec and post RFC (EOD)
- Sanjay: document KMS/HSM integration notes (48h)
- Meg: add metrics hooks and header handling in runtime (PR tomorrow)
ops-bot: Created INF-2340 and assigned to Tess (https://redwood.example/INF-2340)

Leo: One runtime note: keep token TTLs conservative for sensitive workloads (<= 2m). We'll measure perf impact.

Sanjay: +1. We'll instrument and test TTL churn.

Meg (Platform): OK unless anyone objects I will make sidecar-minimal + control-plane-fallback our pattern and update the hosting-adapters doc. Shout if you see a hard blocker.

Tess: No blockers. I'll post a short demo once the stub is up. :thumbsup:
